rows.note: Case-finding is CPSC's incident database CPSRMS (death certificates, news clippings, medical examiners, state/local authorities) plus NEISS deaths, and the report calls the figures 'minimum counts only'. Earlier years as printed: 2022 = 359, 2021 = 390; 2021-2023 total 1,128 (Table 6), average 376 a year (p. 4). Of the 2021-2023 fatalities: pool 95%, spa 5% (Table 8, p. 13); residential 71% (home 51%, family/friend 15%, neighbor 5%), public/community/business 15%, undisclosed 14% (Table 10, p. 16). Fatality years lag the injury years (2023-2025) 'due to a lag in fatality reporting' (p. 4).

rows.scope: Deaths by drowning in recreational boating incidents reported to the U.S. Coast Guard (report label 'Drowning' in Table 1, 'Personal flotation device wear by top five known causes of death'), all ages, United States, calendar 2024; 48 wore a flotation device, 310 did not, 7 unknown. Out of 556 boating deaths from all causes. Only incidents meeting federal reporting criteria on waters of joint federal and state jurisdiction; recreational vessels.
rows.source: U.S. Coast Guard, 2024 Recreational Boating Statistics (24 June 2025), Table 1, p. 7
rows.do_not_add_to: A subset of uscg-boating-2024 (556 deaths, all causes) and, in ICD-10 terms, water-transport drowning (V90/V92) outside W65-W74: do not add to CDC WONDER W65-W74 setting counts, to us-cdc-4500 / us-cdc-4345 / us-total-2022, or to WHO/IHME; do not add to us-location-pool-spa-under15-2023; do not combine with australia-location-2024-25 or uk-waid-2024.
rows.note: The report's '76%' drowning share is 'where cause of death was known' (p. 6); Table 15, p. 33, prints 365 drownings and 191 deaths from other causes, so 365 of all 556 deaths is 66% (own arithmetic within one source). The ledger row uscg-boating-2024 ('3 in 4 drowned') carries the known-cause share. The 2025 edition is listed as 'Pending' on uscgboating.org (checked 15 Oct 2026).

notes: Status partial. The United States does count where people drown, but the count lives in CDC WONDER (NCHS Underlying Cause of Death, final 2018-2024, dataset D176) as ICD-10 codes W65-W74, which are the setting: bathtub (W65 while in, W66 following fall into), swimming pool (W67, W68), natural water (W69, W70), other specified (W73), unspecified (W74); watercraft drownings are V90 and V92, outside the block. NCHS uses exactly this mapping in Data Brief 413 and CDC's risk-factor page cites WONDER for its location shares. WONDER only answers POST requests (API) or an interactive session with the data-use agreement, and neither was reachable from this sandbox (fetch proxy limits GET URL length; shell egress returns 403), so no live figures were obtained and nothing was taken from memory. Query to run (CDC WONDER, 'Underlying Cause of Death, 2018-2024, Single Race'): group results by ICD-10 codes; select codes W65, W66, W67, W68, W69, W70, W73, W74 (and, in a second run, V90 and V92; X71, X92, Y21 if other intents are wanted); year 2024; show totals; measure deaths. One row per code with WONDER's own code titles, and the W65-W74 total row, would complete this task; the 2024 W65-W74 total should sit close to the 2019-2022 totals printed in the Vital Signs MMWR (4,067 / 4,589 / 4,677 / 4,509). The four rows returned are what could be read from primary sources with GET access: (1) CPSC's 2026 pool-or-spa report, children under 15, 2023 = 379 reported drownings (minimum counts from CPSC's incident database, not vital statistics; 71% residential for 2021-2023); (2) the Coast Guard's 2024 statistics, 365 drownings among 556 recreational boating deaths; (3) the NVSS national total as printed in the Vital Signs MMWR, 2022 = 4,509 (W65-W74 + V90 + V92; unintentional only); (4) CDC's own location-by-age statements, which have no year. Definitions, for the reviewer's third check: the NVSS/WONDER figure is accidental (unintentional) drowning only; W65-W74 excludes water transport, which the Vital Signs MMWR adds back as V90 and V92; the CPSC count is pools and spas only, under 15, any location (residential and public), fatality case-finding from death certificates, news clippings and medical examiners; the USCG count is drownings in reportable recreational boating incidents, all ages. None of the three sources can be added to another. Ledger observations (no corrections filed): uscg-boating-2024 says '3 in 4 drowned', which is the report's known-cause share (76%); 365 of all 556 deaths is 66%. us-cdc-4500 ('over 4,500') comes from the same MMWR whose Table 1 prints 4,509 for 2022. The who-data-gaps note lists Australia, the UK and Canada as the countries with a setting split in the ledger; the US does not join that list on this bundle, since no per-setting NVSS counts were obtained.
